summary: Reproduced the independent review's scheduler-budget counterexample on candidate PR https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/pull/3491 at 2ab32e15eddf8f8ba765a382dca23d475f0c6fc3, then preserved its async MP submission and lifecycle cleanup while adding a non-blocking completed-future reap in evictable_size(). The correction resolves review PR https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/pull/3508's circular pin/eviction case without waiting on unfinished stores.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction: a completed MP future was not queried by evictable_size(), leaving its node pinned; the other two cleanup cases passed.

11 focused tests passed for non-blocking submission, budget-boundary reaping, unfinished and query-error pin safety, single-query behavior, eviction/slot reuse, reset, shutdown, submit/future failures, marker/session cleanup, and unchanged IP reconciliation.
Passing-after run of the independent review's three adversarial cases.
Changed source and regression test compile successfully.
No whitespace errors in the consolidated change.

gpu_execution.evidence: The prepared Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 interpreter sees an AMD Instinct MI350X and exposes Event.from_ipc_handle, but LMCache is not installed (find_spec returned None and no distribution metadata exists) and no daemon is available. No real connector, cross-process GPU event, or KV copy was executed.

remaining_limitations: Real LMCache connector/daemon behavior and cross-process GPU event completion on ROCm remain unverified because the frozen environment has no LMCache installation or daemon.
The focused tests use controlled connector futures and validate SGLang lifecycle logic only; they do not establish daemon interoperability or GPU copy correctness.

A query exception is deliberately not treated as completion: the node remains pinned until blocking eviction, reset, or shutdown can reconcile the future, because an exception is not proof that the daemon has finished reading the slots.
